reviews.review: This game tries to be a replacement for Too Human, and well it isn't. Not only is there no map and its easy to get lost or turned around, the mechanics for the player are terrible. No jump function and the weapons suck. Definitely do not buy

I only finished this to nullify the "I didn't like it because I couldn't git gud" stigma.

From all of the Souls-like titles I've completed, between the Deck 13 titles to [b]LET IT DIE[/b], [b]Salt and Sanctuary[/b] to [b]Necropolis[/b], I have not hated playing any of them as much as I did playing [b]Immortal: Unchained[/b].
It may not be the worst game I've ever played, but I would never put myself through this again.

I find referring to [b]Immortal: Unchained[/b] as a Souls-like a bit dubious. It plays like [b]Tom Clancy's The Division[/b] begging to knock up [b]Lords of the Fallen[/b], but they preferred a threesome so they invited [b]Alien Rage[/b] over to form the Eiffel Tower. An action-RPG with guns, RNG drops, high damage intake, stamina management, level system- you get the idea. 

I'll say that [b]Immortal: Unchained[/b] has a decent foundation in gameplay mechanics. Base player movement is clunky; walking is incredibly unresponsive and sluggish. Yet dashing while aiming-down-sights actually works really well, and sprinting feels free. I was surprised that this game had movement that felt this loose. Camera movement can't decide if it's too sensitive or unresponsive. Free-aiming in ADS is incredibly sensitive, especially on controller. I also like that weapon drops and picking up your "souls" is granted by moving over them or just automatically, keeping the flow of gameplay up.

There is also an ostensible amount of lore in [b]Immortal: Unchained[/b], aiding in an elaborate averted prophecy plot about a race war and a slab of stone that controls the universe. However, I do wish that the story was presented in a more digestible way rather than dumping most of it into long expository cutscenes and coarse flavour text.

So what gives?

Enemy variety is anemic. While they have decent designs many of them are reused, repurposed, resized, and revamped numerous times to the point where I pity this game for having a smaller budget. Beyond the main bosses that correlate with the story, every other boss is a variation of a regular enemy. Every enemy has two weakpoints: either their head (remember that free-aiming with ADS is terrible) or their back. 

However, some enemies are [i]special[/i]. Some use sniper rifles that have laser-precise homing bullets or deal hit-scan damage. Some throw up "you can't do anything" shields and move across the map away from you. Some also blatantly teleport spawn in front of you or teleport travel around you. Sometimes these teleporting enemies will also have those super precise sniper rifles and they can also come in droves. There are moments where you'll be fighting multiple teleporting enemies that are always trying to flank you often staggering you, knocking you over, or killing you with their high-damaging weaponry. 

It gets better.

[olist]
[*] Enemies operate by [b]Dark Souls II[/b] enemy logic; they're stubbornly ruthless even while you're healing or using items.

[*] There's no recovery invincibility when you're knocked over or staggered meaning that you can be damaged while still in a stagger or knock-back animation. This damage stacks upon the damage that caused you to topple.

[*] More often than not these enemies possess elemental weapons that inflict status damage. Status effects in [b]Immortal: Unchained[/b] (poison, frost, and burn) occur upon hit without build-up, with minimal warning, and with an indeterminable duration.
[/olist]

It gets better.

You have no method of defense besides dodging however, it's enough to make do with. On the contrary, dodging efficacy is rooted in a particular character skill; it's that weird thing [b]Dark Souls II[/b] did binding dodge-rolling to the Adaptation skill. Except that it's five times weirder in [b]Immortal: Unchained[/b], because five different player mechanics are bound to six different skills: reload speed, healing speed and potency, critical hit damage, normal and special weapon scaling (a skill a piece), and dodge efficiency. 

Obviously none of what I said above is enough to compensate for asserting that "I just suck and I'm a disappointment to my parents", so it's possible to persevere and achieve. 

However, the general game design is spiteful even by Souls-like standards.

Environments are sprawling and elaborate yet "bonfires" in [b]Immortal: Unchained[/b] are far more spread out than they were in [b]Demon's Souls[/b]. There's a fast travel system you unlock halfway through the game where you can unlock "bonfires" as fast travel points for an otherwise expensive sum of "souls".

Consumable items are only obtained through chests and enemy drops, and they don't drop often enough to compensate for their use. There are also no vendors to supply you with extra items, such as in [b]Lords of the Fallen[/b]. "Estus" is very scarce, and can only be upgraded from "armor shrines" that are also hard to come by. Even then you'll be playing through the entire game with about 5 "estus" charges at best (keep in mind everything I've said until now). Armor shrines also offer damage reductions and elemental damage resistance which feel like a cop out to patchwork the maladjusted leveling system.

Weapon scaling rather based on two or three skills, is based on its own arbitrary scaling and skill requirements can be any skill the player has, and very seldom do the requirements match and correlate with other weapons of the same type. Even if they did, weapons will have skill capacity requirements that are nigh impossible to obtain early on and these weapons may never be usable until the endgame. You can't even equip weapons you don't meet skill requirements for. There are perks that can make the boo-boos feel better but these also are random enemy drops and granted by RNG's mercy so progression isn't ever consistent. You will most likely find a better weapon later with a different set of skill requirements. You also cannot reset your skills. 

So starting out this game with its blemishes is just unforgiving however...
IT. GETS. BETTER.

Many of the minor boss fights are already overpowered by the time you fight them early on to the extent where they can pull a one-hit kill attack out of their pocket at any time. If that's not enough, almost every boss relies on the tactic of phoning friends in, including elite enemies turning otherwise fair fights into [i]A Clockwork Orange[/i], the player portraying the role of Mrs. Alexander. What's baffling is that the main boss fights don't rely on backup, are very easy to beat, and are boring to fight. The game doesn't even have the damn courtesy to warp you to the central hub or offer a "bonfire" after completing an area, forcing you to backtrack through runbacks worse than the ones from [b]Dark Souls II[/b], or use a "homeward bone" which are extremely rare to find.

The foundation for [b]Immortal: Unchained[/b] is solid enough to become an average yet fun, free-flowing, third-person shooter partially akin to [b]Vanquish[/b], if it weren't so mired in its aspirations to be a Souls-like through dodgy game design and jank.
If you read this long diatribe to this point, I thank you reader and offer you a pat on the back but just heed my caution:

[i]Only play this if you wish to unleash demons from within yourself[/i].
